The '''TI-84 Plus series''' is a line of [[graphing calculator]]s produced by [[Texas Instruments]]. They are ubiquitous in the [[Education in the United States|American education system]], and have historically been considered the ''de facto'' standard in [[Grade school mathematics|grade school math]]. The series has also amassed a significant [[hobbyist]] following, along with a large library of community-developed applications, for its support of [[assembly language]] and [[TI-BASIC]] programs.

The family was superseded by the [[TI-84 Plus CE series|TI-84 Plus CE]] series in 2015; of the original series, only the TI-84 Plus is still in production, the Silver Edition and C Silver Edition having been discontinued that same year. However, they remain popular in the [[United States]], with the TI-84 Plus being issued by schools more than 20 years after its introduction.

Beginning from around 2011, the series has received media attention from technology publications due to hobbyist app releases for the platform, such as an unofficial [[ChatGPT]] client, a [[web browser]], and a [[Neural network (machine learning)|neural network]]. In recent years, however, the TI-84 Plus has been increasingly criticized for its antiquated technology and poor [[Value (economics)|value for money]], with critics claiming that its continued sale is a result of Texas Instruments' calculator [[monopoly]].

==Editions==

=== TI-84 Plus ===
The original TI-84 Plus{{Efn|The use of "Plus" in the calculator's name is because the TI-84 Plus directly replaced the [[TI-83 Plus]], which was itself a more powerful version of the [[TI-83]]. Unlike its predecessor, however, the TI-84 Plus does not have an "original" or "non-Plus" variant.<ref name="83plus">{{Cite web |title=TI-83 Plus |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-83PLUS.htm |last=Bollman |first=Mark |access-date=2025-11-11 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-84PLUS.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Texas Instruments Graphing and Symbolic Calculators, List. |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum |url=http://www.datamath.org/Album_Graph.htm |access-date=2025-12-11 |website=www.datamath.org}}</ref>}} was released in 2004 as an upgrade to the [[TI-83 series#TI-83 Plus|TI-83 Plus]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |first= |title=TI-84 Plus series: Timeline |url=https://education.ti.com/en/snapapp/timeline |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=education.ti.com |publisher=TI Education Hub |language=en}}</ref> Its keyboard layout and user interface are identical to that of its predecessor, and it is [[Backward compatibility|backwards compatible]] with older TI-BASIC programs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus Specifications |url=http://tifreakware.net/tutorials/83p/spec84p.htm |access-date=2025-12-11 |website=tifreakware.net}}</ref> Despite this, it has significantly improved hardware; its CPU, the [[Zilog Z80]], is 2.5 times as fast as the one in the TI-83 Plus, its display is of a higher [[Contrast (vision)|contrast]], and it has three times as much [[flash memory]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name="83plus"></ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-84PLUS.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref> 

The TI-84 Plus introduced a [[real-time clock]] and a [[USB-B|mini-USB]] data transfer port.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus - ticalc.org |url=https://www.ticalc.org/basics/calculators/ti-84plus.html |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=www.ticalc.org |publisher=TICalc}}</ref> The USB port is [[USB On-The-Go]] compliant, allowing the TI-84 Plus to connect to—and exchange data with—another calculator; Texas Instruments calls this feature Communication Link.<ref name="guidebook">{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus Guidebook |url=https://education.ti.com/html/eguides/graphing/84Plus/PDFs/TI-84-Plus-guidebook_EN.pdf |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=education.ti.com |publisher=Texas Instruments |language=en}}</ref> The TI-84 Plus can also connect to a computer to transfer programs and files using Texas Instruments' proprietary program, TI-Connect.<ref name="connect">{{Cite web |title=TI Connect™ Software |url=https://education.ti.com/en/products/computer-software/ti-connect-sw |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=education.ti.com |publisher=TI Education Hub |language=en}}</ref>

An all-white variant of the TI-84 Plus was introduced in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=White TI-84 Plus |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum |url=http://datamath.org/Graphing/TI-84PLUS_WH.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=datamath.org}}</ref> Currently, the calculator is still in production and issued by schools around the United States, required by some institutions, and seen as the standard option by many; critics argue that the enduring prevalence of the TI-84 Plus—which is considerably less powerful than a smartphone, yet still costs more than some—has hindered innovation in calculator technology and is a result of [[monopoly]]. They also claim that Texas Instruments exploits this by [[Price gouging|keeping prices]] at a level roughly twice that of competing calculators.<ref>{{Cite news |last=McFarland |first=Matt |date=2014-09-02 |title=The unstoppable TI-84 Plus: How an outdated calculator still holds a monopoly on classrooms |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/innovations/wp/2014/09/02/the-unstoppable-ti-84-plus-how-an-outdated-calculator-still-holds-a-monopoly-on-classrooms/ |access-date=2025-10-24 |newspaper=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Anderson |first=Tristan |date=2024-02-29 |title=TI's Calculator Empire: The (Un)Stoppable TI-84 |url=https://bhsblueprint.org/showcase/2024/02/29/tis-calculator-empire-the-unstoppable-ti-84/ |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=BHS Blueprint}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith IV |first=Jack |date=September 28, 2015 |title=Remember Your Old Graphing Calculator? It Still Costs a Fortune — Here's Why |url=https://www.mic.com/articles/125829/your-old-texas-instruments-graphing-calculator-still-costs-a-fortune-heres-why |access-date=2025-11-12 |website=Mic |language=en}}</ref>

=== TI-84 Plus Silver Edition ===
[[File:TI 84 Plus Silver Edition.svg|thumb|TI-84 Plus Silver Edition]]
The TI-84 Plus Silver Edition (SE) was introduced on January 7, 2004 as an upgrade to the [[TI-83 series#TI-83 Plus Silver Edition|TI-83 Plus Silver Edition]]. It features 24&nbsp;KB of user-available RAM; the calculator technically has 128&nbsp;KB—48&nbsp;KB in newer revisions—but the operating system was never updated to utilize it. It has 1.5&nbsp;MB of user-accessible ROM, more than three times the 480&nbsp;KB in the TI-84 Plus. It came preloaded with 30 applications.<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus Silver Edition |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-84PLUS_SE.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-10-28 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref>

The Silver Edition has interchangeable faceplates, and new, colored faceplates were available for purchase at Texas Instruments' online store.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Solution 19189: Using the TI-84 Plus Silver Edition Faceplate on the TI-83 Plus Family Graphing Calculators. |url=https://education.ti.com/en/customer-support/knowledge-base/ti-83-84-plus-family/general-information/19189 |access-date=2025-10-30 |website=education.ti.com |publisher=TI Education Hub |language=en}}</ref> It was discontinued in 2015, making the TI-84 Plus the only currently produced calculator in the series.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |author=Tech Powered Dad |title=The Evolving TI-84 Plus Platform |url=https://www.techpoweredmath.com/ti-84-models-discontinued/ |access-date=September 2, 2025 |website=www.techpoweredmath.com}}</ref>

=== TI-84 Plus C Silver Edition ===

[[File:The proposed Ti-84+ C Edition SE.jpg | thumb | right | TI 84 Plus C Silver Edition]]
The TI-84 Plus C Silver Edition (C SE) was released in 2013 as the first Z80-based Texas Instruments graphing calculator with a color screen.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus C Silver Edition |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-84PLUS_CSE.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=October 28, 2025 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref>

It introduced a 320-by-240 pixel color screen, a modified version of the TI-84 Plus's 2.55MP operating system, and a removable 1200&nbsp;mAh rechargeable lithium-ion battery.<ref>{{cite web |last=Mitchell |first=Christopher |date=February 20, 2013 |title=Hands-On with the TI-84 Plus C Silver Edition: Full Review - Cemetech - News |url=https://www.cemetech.net/news.php?id=567 |access-date=21 February 2013 |publisher=Cemetech}}</ref><ref name=":8" /> It was praised for its high-resolution color screen, which added new capabilities such as the ability to graph multiple simultaneous functions in different colors.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Tech Powered Dad |date=March 18, 2013 |title=TI-84 Plus C Silver Edition Review |url=https://www.techpoweredmath.com/ti-84c-review/ |access-date=October 27, 2025 |website=www.techpoweredmath.com}}</ref> The C Silver Edition would not be Texas Instruments' last foray into color-screen calculators for the student market; the TI-84 Plus CE was introduced—with an upgraded CPU—two years later.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus CE |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-84PLUS_CE.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=October 30, 2025 |website=www.datamath.org}}</ref> The C Silver Edition was discontinued a few months after the launch of the CE.<ref name=":4" />

==Software==

=== Programs and applications ===
The TI-84 Plus series supports both programs and applications. Programs are written by the user; some programs, like those written in TI-BASIC, are [[Interpreted (programming languages)|interpreted]] during execution and can thus be edited directly on the calculator.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Solution 10442: Executing TI-Basic and Assembly (ASM) Programs on the TI-86. |url=https://education.ti.com/en/customer-support/knowledge-base/other-graphing/product-usage/10442 |access-date=2025-11-12 |website=education.ti.com |publisher=TI Education Hub |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Solution 29090: Stopping, Breaking or Ending a TI-Basic Program on Texas Instruments Graphing Calculators |url=https://education.ti.com/en/customer-support/knowledge-base/ti-83-84-plus-family/product-usage/29090 |access-date=2025-11-12 |website=education.ti.com |language=en}}</ref> Applications (also called ''Flash applications''{{Efn|The "Flash" in "Flash application" does not refer to [[Adobe Flash]]; it signifies that the application uses Texas Instruments' FLASH technology.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Solution 11892: Running a Program from the Archive Memory on a Graphing Calculator with FLASH Technology. |url=https://education.ti.com/en/customer-support/knowledge-base/ti-83-84-plus-family/product-usage/11892 |access-date=2025-11-12 |website=education.ti.com |publisher=TI Education Hub |language=en}}</ref>}}) are stored in the calculator's ROM; these tend to be more complex than standard programs, and are usually from Texas Instruments themselves.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Solution 11410: Benefits of Calculator Software Applications (Apps) Over User-created Programs. |url=https://education.ti.com/en/customer-support/knowledge-base/ti-83-84-plus-family/general-information/11410 |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=education.ti.com |publisher=TI Education Hub |language=en}}</ref> Officially, two [[programming languages]] are supported: TI-BASIC and [[Assembly language|Z80 assembly]].<ref name="guidebook"></ref> However, there are unofficial, community-developed languages—such as the ''Axe Parser''—made specifically for the TI-84 Plus series.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Horowitz |first=Kevin |title=Axe Parser 1.2.2 - ticalc.org |url=https://www.ticalc.org/archives/files/fileinfo/456/45659.html |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=www.ticalc.org |publisher=TICalc}}</ref>

The series has a significant [[hobbyist]] following, and a wide variety of official and community-made software has been developed for it over the years.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hilliard |first=George |date=2021-10-06 |title=The Insane Innovation of TI Calculator Hobbyists |url=https://www.thirtythreeforty.net/posts/2021/10/ti-calculator-innovation/ |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=www.thirtythreeforty.net |language=en-us}}</ref> These include video games, math programs, educational tools, and graphing software.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI-83/84 Plus Files (not including the TI-84 Plus C Silver Edition/CE) - ticalc.org |url=https://www.ticalc.org/pub/83plus/ |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=www.ticalc.org |publisher=TICalc}}</ref> In 2011, an unofficial [[web browser]], ''Gossamer'', was released for the platform,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Biggs |first=John |date=2011-07-25 |title=Gossamer Web Browser Runs On Your Graphing Calculator |url=https://techcrunch.com/2011/07/25/gossamer-web-browser-runs-on-your-graphing-calculator/ |access-date=2025-11-13 |website=TechCrunch |language=en-US}}</ref> and in recent years, programmers have created internet-based programs like a [[ChatGPT]] client, graphical [[ray-casting]] software, and a [[Neural network (machine learning)|neural network]] that incorporates primitive [[artificial intelligence]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |first=Benj|last=Edwards |title=Secret calculator hack brings ChatGPT to the TI-84, enabling easy cheating |url=https://arstechnica.com/information-technology/2024/09/secret-calculator-hack-brings-chatgpt-to-the-ti-84-enabling-easy-cheating/ |access-date=December 1, 2025 |magazine=Wired |via=Ars Technica|language=en-US |issn=1059-1028}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Davidson |first=Patrick |title=Patrick Davidson's TI-84 Plus CE / TI-83 Premium CE page |url=https://www.ocf.berkeley.edu/~pad/ti84ce.html |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=www.ocf.berkeley.edu}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Bild |first=Nick |date=July 2025 |title=An AI-Powered Spell Checker for the TI-84 |url=https://www.hackster.io/news/an-ai-powered-spell-checker-for-the-ti-84-ddc3f5d8706b |access-date=2025-10-28 |website=Hackster.io |language=en}}</ref> These developments have attracted the attention of technology publications.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Marcin |first=Tim |date=2024-09-23 |title=See ChatGPT run on a TI-84 graphing calculator |url=https://mashable.com/article/chatgpt-ti-84-graphing-calculator |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=Mashable |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Harper |first=Christopher |date=2024-09-22 |url=https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/artificial-intelligence/modder-hacks-chatgpt-other-apps-onto-ti-84-calculator-creates-the-ultimate-cheating-device |access-date=2025-10-29 |website=Tom's Hardware |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-07-17 |last=Chung |first=Jackson |title=This AI-Powered TI-84 is Now a Calculator That Spells Success, Literally === Operating systems ===
There have been eight [[operating system]] releases for the monochrome-display calculators in the series, which include the TI-84 Plus, the Silver Edition, and their respective variants.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5" /><ref name=":6" /> There have been two releases for the C Silver Edition.<ref name=":12">{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus C Silver Edition - ticalc.org |url=https://www.ticalc.org/basics/calculators/ti-84plus-cse.html |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=www.ticalc.org |publisher=TICalc}}</ref><ref name=":8" /> TI-84 Plus series calculators can run custom [[Shell (computing)|user interface shells]], such as ''MirageOS'' and ''Doors CS''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Main Page |url=https://dcs.cemetech.net/ |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=dcs.cemetech.net |publisher=Doors CS, hosted on Cemetech |language=en-us}}</ref> In addition, calculators with an older [[bootloader]] can run custom operating systems like ''KnightOS''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI-83/84 Plus Operating Systems - ticalc.org |url=https://www.ticalc.org/pub/83plus/os/ |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=www.ticalc.org |publisher=TICalc}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Homepage |url=https://knightos.org |publisher=KnightOS Team}}</ref>

=== Linking software ===
Texas Instruments develops the TI-Connect linking software, which hosts a number of sub-programs (called ''software tools'') to manage TI-84 Plus series calculators.<ref name="connect" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=TI-Connect Guidebook |url=https://education.ti.com/html/eguides/connectivity/TI-Connect/EN/TI-Connect-windows-guidebook-en.html |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=education.ti.com |publisher=TI Education Hub |language=en}}</ref>
{| class="wikitable"
|+
!Tool
!Function
|-
|ScreenCapture
|Capture and save a still of a calculator's screen.
|-
|DeviceInformation
|Generate an information report of a calculator, which includes details such as its model, available storage, and installed applications.
|-
|DataEditor
|Modify variables on a calculator, such as numbers, lists, and [[Matrix (mathematics)|matrixes]].
|-
|DeviceExplorer
|Copy files to and from a calculator, install programs and applications, and create file groups.
|-
|OS Downloader
|Upgrade or downgrade the operating system on a calculator.
|-
|Backup/Restore
|Create and restore complete calculator backups, including RAM, applications, and flash memory.
|}
Texas Instruments' newer program for the [[TI-84 Plus CE series]] calculators, TI-Connect CE, is [[Backward compatibility|backwards-compatible]] with the TI-84 Plus series; it can be used in place of TI-Connect.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=TI Connect™ CE Software Application |url=https://education.ti.com/en/products/computer-software/ti-connect-ce-sw |access-date=2025-09-05 |website=education.ti.com |publisher=TI Education Hub |language=en}}</ref> TI-Connect is compatible with [[Windows XP]] and above,<ref name="connect" /> while TI-Connect CE is compatible with [[Windows 10]] and above.<ref name=":3" />

There are multiple third-party linking programs compatible with the TI-84 Plus series; most were developed for [[Obsolescence#Technical obsolescence|archaic platforms]] like the [[Amiga|Commodore Amiga]], the [[Atari 8-bit computers|Atari]], and [[MS-DOS]], and cannot be run on modern computers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Linking - ticalc.org |url=https://www.ticalc.org/basics/linking/software.html |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=www.ticalc.org |publisher=TICalc}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Dube |first=Ryan |date=2018-02-21 |title=Why Can't 64-Bit Operating Systems Run 16-Bit Apps? |url=https://www.makeuseof.com/tag/why-cant-64-bit-run-16-bit/ |access-date=2025-11-04 |website=MUO |language=en}}</ref> However, one of these programs—known as ''TiLP''{{Efn|TiLP stands for "TiLP is a Linking Program", which is a [[recursive acronym]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Features |url=http://lpg.ticalc.org/prj_tilp/features.html |publisher=The TiLP Project |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=lpg.ticalc.org}}</ref> The original TiLP (known as TiLP-1) was supplanted by TiLP II (also known as TiLP-2) around mid-2006.<ref>{{Cite web |title=News|url=http://lpg.ticalc.org/prj_tilp/news.html |publisher=The TiLP Project |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=lpg.ticalc.org}}</ref> TiLP, as used here, refers to TiLP II.}}—is more recent and supports [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]], [[macOS]], and [[Linux]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Homepage |url=http://lpg.ticalc.org/prj_tilp/ |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=lpg.ticalc.org |publisher=The TiLP Project}}</ref>

== Equipment ==
Texas Instruments has released a variety of equipment for its graphing calculators. Even though only the Calculator-Based Ranger 2 features a USB port, the TI-84 Plus series can connect to older Texas Instruments equipment using its serial link port.<ref name=":5" /> Since the newer [[TI-84 Plus CE series]] does not have this port, it is not compatible with most of this equipment.<ref name=":2" />

=== ViewScreen ===
{{Main|ViewScreen}}

The ViewScreen is an LCD panel and [[Projector|projection system]] that mirrors the display of a calculator; it was first introduced in 1993, and there have been several models since. Unlike most other equipment, it does not use the link port.{{Efn|''Link port'', as used here, refers to the serial "I/O" link port on all TI-84 Plus series calculators, not the ViewScreen display port.}} However, there is a dongle—the ''Presentation Link Adapter''—that allows a standard TI-84 Plus to connect to a ViewScreen panel.<ref>{{Cite web |title=ViewScreen |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-VSP82_LTA93.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-11-14 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref>

=== Presenter ===
The Presenter, introduced in 2003, is an alternative piece of calculator screen display equipment; instead of using a [[wikt:proprietary|proprietary]] display panel and overhead projection system like the ViewScreen, the Presenter connects to an existing display device—such as a television or [[interactive whiteboard]]—using either an [[RF modulator]] or [[composite video]] input. Since it uses the same [[communication protocol]] as the ViewScreen, it is compatible with both the Presentation Link Adapter and ViewScreen variants of the TI-84 Plus.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI Presenter |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/Presenter.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref>

=== Calculator-Based Laboratory ===
The Calculator-Based Laboratory (CBL), a general purpose [[data acquisition]] unit, was introduced in 1994. It collects information from several types of [[Modular design|modular]] sensors by [[Vernier Science Education|Vernier, Inc.]]—at a speed of up to 10,000 data points per second—and sends it to a calculator via link cable, which records and graphs the data. It also features a display and basic firmware of its own for standalone data processing.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Calculator-Based Laboratory |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/CBL.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-11-14 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref> In 1999, the CBL was superseded by the CBL 2, which lacked a display for standalone use but introduced flash memory and increased the single-channel sample rate to 50,000 data points per second.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Calculator-Based Laboratory 2 |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/CBL2.htm |access-date=2025-11-14 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref>

=== Calculator-Based Ranger ===
The Calculator-Based Ranger (CBR), introduced in 1997, is, like the CBL, a data acquisition unit, but features a single built-in sonic sensor instead of multiple unique modular ones. It measures distances by emitting and receiving an [[Ultrasound|ultrasonic pulse]], and then calculating the distance traveled by performing a [[Speed of sound|speed-of-sound]] calculation using its [[microprocessor]]. It then stores this information in a list—which can contain up to 512 data points—and transfers that to a calculator via link cable.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Calculator-Based Ranger |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/CBR.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-11-14 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref> The CBR was replaced by the CBR 2 in 2004, which added a USB port for faster data transfer with the TI-84 Plus series.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Calculator-Based Ranger 2 |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/CBR2.htm |access-date=2025-11-14 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref>

=== Orion Talking Graphing Calculator ===
The Orion TI-84 Plus Talking Graphing Calculator is a detachable accessory for the TI-84 Plus produced by Texas Instruments in collaboration with [[Orbit Research]] and the [[American Printing House for the Blind]]. It adds general accessibility features—such as speech navigation—to the TI-84 Plus, and is able to read out the contents of the calculator's display using [[speech synthesis]]. It uses its own power source, a rechargeable battery, instead of drawing power from the calculator itself.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Orion TI-84 Plus Talking Graphing Calculator User's Guide |url=https://tech.aph.org/Orion%20TI-84%20Plus%20Documents/gc_doc.htm |access-date=2025-11-17 |website=tech.aph.org |publisher=APH Tech}}</ref>

== Variants ==

=== TI-84 Plus EZ-Spot ===
The TI-84 Plus EZ-Spot series, also known as the School editions and the School Property editions, are variants of TI-84 Plus series calculators produced by Texas Instruments and only made available for schools to purchase.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus (EZ-Spot) |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-84PLUS_Y.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=www.datamath.org}}</ref> They have the words "School Property" emblazoned on their faceplate and are accented yellow; this easily distinguishable design was chosen in an effort to prevent theft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus Graphing Calculator |url=https://education.ti.com/en/products/calculators/graphing-calculators/ti-84-plus |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=education.ti.com |publisher=TI Education Hub |language=en}}</ref> The TI-84 Plus Silver Edition and C Silver Edition also have EZ-Spot variants.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus Silver Edition (EZ-Spot) |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-84PLUS_SE_Y.htm |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=www.datamath.org}}</ref>

=== TI-84 Plus Silver Edition VSC ===
The TI-84 Plus Silver Edition ViewScreen Calculator, also known as the TI-84 Plus Silver Edition VSC, is a variant of the TI-84 Plus Silver Edition intended for educational use.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus Silver Edition (ViewScreen Calculator) |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-84PLUS_SE_VSC.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-10-30 |website=www.datamath.org}}</ref> It has a display output that allows it to connect to a [[ViewScreen]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI ViewScreen 82 |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-VSP82.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-10-30 |website=www.datamath.org}}</ref>

=== TI-84 Plus T ===
The TI-84 Plus T is a variant of the TI-84 Plus; it was introduced in 2015 by Texas Instruments, exclusive to the Netherlands. This variant is similar to the rest of the series, but features an LED to indicate whether or not the calculator is in [[Exam mode|press-to-test mode]]. The hardware of the TI-84 Plus T is similar to the TI-84 Plus Silver Edition, but the TI-84 Plus T is no longer able to run the [[Assembly language|assembler]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus T |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-84PLUS-T.htm |last=Andréani |first=Xavier |access-date=2025-10-27 |website=www.datamath.org}}</ref>

=== TI-84 Pocket.fr and Plus Pocket SE ===
The TI-84 Pocket.fr{{Efn|This is the only mentioned TI-84 Plus series calculator to not have the ''Plus'' in its name. However, it does still have flash memory, and is still considered part of the TI-84 Plus family due to it being a TI-84 Plus derivative.<ref name="POCKET_FR">{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Pocket.fr |url=http://www.datamath.org/Graphing/TI-84POCKET_FR.htm |last=Woerner |first=Joerg |access-date=2025-11-14 |website=www.datamath.org |publisher=Datamath Calculator Museum}}</ref>}} was introduced in 2011 as a miniaturized variant of the TI-84 Plus for the French market.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Pocket.fr |url=https://education.ti.com/educationportal/sites/FRANCE/productDetail/fr_TI-84Pocket.html |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110403005741/https://education.ti.com/educationportal/sites/FRANCE/productDetail/fr_TI-84Pocket.html |archive-date=April 3, 2011 |access-date=June 6, 2020 |publisher=TI Education Hub, France |language=fr}}</ref> It was the first region-specific calculator in the TI-84 Plus series.<ref name="POCKET_FR" /> A year later, the TI-84 Plus Pocket SE was introduced as a miniaturized variant of the TI-84 Plus Silver Edition for the Asian market.<ref>{{Cite web |title=TI-84 Plus Pocket SE |url=http://education.ti.com/educationportal/sites/ASIA/productDetail/asia_ti84p_pocket_se.html |url-status=bot: unknown |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426211449/http://education.ti.com/educationportal/sites/ASIA/productDetail/asia_ti84p_pocket_se.html |archive-date=26 April 2012 |access-date=3 January 2012 |publisher=TI Education Hub, Asia}}</ref>
